title: Lattice-shell form is independent of the material, being moulded on vesicles

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Lattice-shell form is independent of the material, being moulded on vesicles

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Spherical hexagonal lattice shells are equally regular whether made of silica (oceanic Radiolaria), strontium sulphate (Acantharia) or an organic chitin-like substance (Clathrulina), showing that their form comes from moulding on an underlying vesicular structure, not from the material.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. IX: On Concretions, Spicules, and Spicular Skeletons

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: This is only another proof (if proof be needed) that the peculiar conformation of these little skeletons is not due to the material of which they are composed, but to the moulding of that material upon an underlying vesicular structure.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter IX, “On Concretions, Spicules, and Spicular Skeletons”; topic “Radiolarian lattice shells”. Scope: Radiolaria and Heliozoa with lattice skeletons of different composition

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch09-15: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.49

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Material-independence of gross form is measurable from existing morphology. The stronger causal inference to an underlying vesicular structure remains poorly discriminated without developmental observations.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare lattice regularity and topology across silica-, celestite- and organic-skeleton taxa using standardized images, then test whether material predicts form after phylogeny and size are controlled. Demonstrating an underlying vesicular template requires direct developmental imaging rather than cross-material convergence alone.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Cross-material convergence is not unique evidence for vesicle moulding.

The groups differ in phylogeny, ecology and scale.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: A common regularity metric across the three named materials is a straightforward test of the independence claim. Silica lattices are well imaged; strontium-sulphate and organic lattices are mostly in separate papers and drawings. The available sample can compare a limited set of species, and phylogenetic confounding keeps a positive result from isolating the mould as the cause.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Apply one regularity metric, such as mesh-angle variance or deviation from a spherical hex net, to silica radiolarian lattices, strontium-sulphate acantharian skeletons and organic Clathrulina lattices. Equal regularity supports material-independence; regularity that tracks chemistry refutes it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Acantharia dissolve and Clathrulina is not a focus of the radiolarian image archives, so the three materials are unequally documented.

Chemistry is confounded with clade, so equal regularity need not mean a shared vesicular mould.
